title: Measures to Develop Baseline Artificial Intelligence Literacy of Students
what_it_is: Measures to Develop Baseline Artificial Intelligence Literacy of Students

sections.label: AI Student Outreach Programme questions
sections.summary: An MP asks about applicant numbers, applicant breakdown by institution type, and plans to increase take-up of the Artificial Intelligence Student Outreach Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students have applied to join the Artificial Intelligence Student Outreach Programme; (b) what is the respective percentage of applicants who are from (i) secondary schools (ii) polytechnics (iii) Integrated Programme schools and (iv) junior colleges; and (c) whether there are plans to increase the take-up rate of the programme.

sections.label: 2023 programme applicant breakdown
sections.summary: In 2023, close to 17,000 students applied, with 11% from polytechnics, 52% from secondary schools, 11% from IP schools and 3% from junior colleges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In 2023, close to 17,000 students applied to join the programme, with the breakdown of applicants as follows: (a) 11% from the polytechnics; (b) 52% from the secondary schools; (c) 11% from the IP schools; and (d) 3% from the junior colleges.

sections.label: AI tools and governance in IHLs
sections.summary: IHLs use AI tools in specific domains, have governance frameworks for ethical AI use, and working adults can take AI-related SkillsFuture courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The IHLs also incorporate the use of AI tools in specific domains to ensure students understand the risks that AI poses, such as the potential to perpetuate misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: They also have governance frameworks to ensure the ethical and responsible use of AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Beyond our schools and IHLs, working adults can take up AI-related SkillsFuture courses to become smart and secure users of AI in their respective industries.

sections.label: AI adaptive learning system for mathematics
sections.summary: An AI-enabled adaptive learning system for mathematics has been available on the Singapore Student Learning Space for Primary 5 topics since 2023, with more topics to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At another level, we also use an AI-enabled adaptive learning system (ALS) for mathematics that has been made available through our Singapore Student Learning Space (SLS) for Primary 5-level topics since 2023, with more topics to be progressively rolled out in the next two years.

sections.label: Habits beyond school premises
sections.summary: The speaker hopes these habits apply beyond school premises throughout students' lives and says Mr Ong's suggestion will be taken into account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Hopefully, these habits apply to them not just within the school premises, but also, throughout their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will take into account Mr Ong's suggestion.

sections.label: Ethical AI learning with technical use
sections.summary: MOE agrees learning to use AI is important but ethical use is more important, and will always couple technical AI learning with ethical AI learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, we certainly agree that learning to use AI is important, but learning to use AI ethically is even more important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For us, from MOE's position, we will always couple the learning of the technical use of AI with the ethical use of AI.

sections.label: Mathematics and logical thinking importance
sections.summary: The passage states that mathematics, logical thinking and computational skills are very important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, the importance of mathematics, logical thinking, computational skills – these are very important.

sections.label: PISA results and computational thinking
sections.summary: Students did well in PISA in logical thinking and computational thinking traits.

sentences.text: Even in the recent Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results, we are glad that our students have done well in terms of their ability to think logically and to exhibit traits of computational thinking.

sections.label: Equal opportunities and deepfake education
sections.summary: The passage asks whether opportunities are evenly available across socio-economic backgrounds and whether youths are educated about deepfake risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister assure us that the opportunities he described in his answer are evenly available for students across households of diverse social economic backgrounds?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Recently, the Prime Minister, himself, mentioned the risk of deepfake videos.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Are we educating our younger generation to be mindful of deepfakes, the risk of being tricked as well as the risk of deepfake technology being abused against peers in unethical ways?

sections.label: Home access and digital divide
sections.summary: MOE ensured students have laptops, tablets, computers and bandwidth at home, running online and offline systems to avoid a digital divide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, we made sure that even if the students do not come to school, they have access to laptops, tablets and computers so that they can learn at home and we even made sure that they have access to the bandwidth necessary to support the working of this laptop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, our teachers actually run two systems in parallel whereby we have online access and also offline, back-in-the-school access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is MOE's commitment to make sure that, through the use of technology, we do not end up with a digital divide but, instead, we use technology to democratise the access to the best material available to all students.

sections.label: Trusted information sources
sections.summary: The passage states work is ongoing with MCI and other Ministries, with trusted information sources at the core of the democratic system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer is yes, we are working closely with MCI and other Ministries to do this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At the crux of it is whether we can have trusted sources of information, which goes to the core of our democratic system.
